title: Canonical polynomial-module localization and its good locus
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\geq0$, and $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $M$ be a $P$-module. For $f\in R$, put $R_f=R[1/f]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and $T_f=\{C(f)^a:a\geq0\}\subset P$, where $C:R\to P$ is the constant-polynomial map. Use the fraction module $T_f^{-1}M$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], canonically identified with the localization of the underlying $R$-module at $f$ by $m/C(f)^a\leftrightarrow m/f^a$. The canonical identification $T_f^{-1}P=R_f[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ gives it the module action $(p/C(f)^a)\cdot(m/C(f)^b)=(pm)/C(f)^{a+b}$; in particular $x_i(m/f^a)=(x_im)/f^a$. Its $R_f$-action is restriction along constant polynomials. Define the polynomial-module good locus $G_R(M)\subset\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] to be the union of $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$ over all $f\in R$ for which this localized module is free over $R_f$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module] and finitely presented over $R_f[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Freeness permits arbitrary, including infinite and empty, bases. No reducedness, finiteness, or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed.
